new.title: Walk across the Krämerbrücke, lined with houses
new.desc: A bridge over the Gera first mentioned in 1117; the stone version was completed in 1325 and the present houses date from the rebuild after the 1472 fire. Shops and workshops still occupy the timber-framed houses.
new.tip: Come early morning to beat the crowds; the Stiftung Krämerbrücke exhibit at No. 31 has a 1:100 model.

new.title: Climb the Domstufen to Erfurt Cathedral
new.desc: The Romanesque basilica begun in 1154 became a Gothic cathedral with famed choir windows from about 1370 to 1420. Its Gloriosa bell, cast in 1497, is the largest free-swinging medieval bell in the world.
new.tip: Visit together with the neighbouring Severikirche; the Gloriosa rings mainly on high feast days.

new.title: See the Severus sarcophagus in St. Severi
new.desc: The Gothic hall church on the Domberg holds relics of Saint Severus brought to Erfurt in 836. Look for the 1510 Marienaltar and the alabaster Archangel Michael relief of 1467.
new.tip: Check opening times on the parish website; combine with the cathedral next door.

new.title: Walk the ramparts of Zitadelle Petersberg
new.desc: One of the largest and best preserved town fortresses in Central Europe, a Baroque citadel built from the 17th century above the old town. The grounds give views over the cathedral hill.
new.tip: Guided tours of the underground tunnels are offered; wear sturdy shoes on the cobbles.

new.title: Discover the Alte Synagoge and the Erfurt Treasure
new.desc: A medieval synagogue in the courtyard between Fischmarkt and Michaelisstraße, now a museum holding the Jewish treasure found in 1998. Together with the mikveh it became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in September 2023.
new.tip: The museum is part of Jüdisches Leben in Erfurt; check juedisches-leben.erfurt.de for hours.

new.title: Follow Martin Luther at the Augustinerkloster
new.desc: Luther lived here as a monk from 1505 to 1511 and said his first Mass on 2 May 1507. The permanent exhibition Frust und Freiheit opened in March 2025.
new.tip: Check augustinerkloster.de for hours and tours.

new.title: Admire the painted stairwells of Erfurt Rathaus
new.desc: Neogothic town hall on the Fischmarkt, built 1869 to 1882 by Theodor Sommer. The stairwells and Festsaal carry history paintings of Erfurt and Luther.
new.tip: The painted stairwells are freely accessible to visitors.

new.title: Visit the working Neue Mühle by the Gera
new.desc: The last functioning mill of what were once 60 in the city, a museum of the Stadtmuseum Erfurt since 1992. Its original water wheel still drives a generator.
new.tip: See stadtmuseum-erfurt.de for opening days.

new.title: Eat Thüringer Klöße and roulade at Feuerkugel
new.desc: Gasthaus on Michaelisstraße serving regional Thuringian cooking: Rinderroulade, Thüringer Bratwurst and homemade dumplings. Reviewers also single out the Erfurt black beer meat with Klöße.
new.tip: Mains cost roughly 20 to 30 euros; book for evenings.

new.title: Try Sauerbraten with Klöße at Naumburgischer Keller
new.desc: Half-timbered house with a vaulted stone cellar on Michaelisstraße. Guests praise the roulade, sauerbraten and Thüringer Klöße.
new.tip: Ask for a table in the vaulted cellar.
new.q: Haus zum Naumburgischen Keller, Michaelisstraße 49, Erfurt

new.title: Order game with Klöße at Wirtshaus Christoffel
new.desc: Wirtshaus on Michaelisstraße known for Thuringian dumplings served with game, plus Rostbrätel on the menu.
new.tip: Pick the dumpling dishes over the grill plates.

new.title: Eat Rinderroulade with Klöße at Zum Wenigemarkt 13
new.desc: Restaurant on the Wenigemarkt serving Thuringian cooking such as Rinderroulade with Klöße and Sauerbraten, next to the Krämerbrücke.
new.tip: Sit outside on the square in summer.

new.title: Taste handmade truffles at Goldhelm on the Krämerbrücke
new.desc: Goldhelm Schokoladen Manufaktur started in 2005 in the historic Haus zum güldenen Helm on the bridge. The Krämerbrücke truffles and pralines are the usual picks.
new.tip: A sister ice cream shop, Eiskrämer, is at Kreuzgasse 5.

new.title: Sip hand-roasted coffee at Bohnea on the Fischmarkt
new.desc: Café and roastery serving hand-roasted specialty coffee and cake in the old town, steps from the Rathaus.
new.tip: Fischmarkt 6; try a filter coffee with a slice of cake.

new.title: Have cake with a cathedral view at Café Hilgenfeld
new.desc: Independent café on the Domplatz ranked among Erfurt's top cafés, with seating facing the cathedral square.
new.tip: Quietest in the morning outside Christmas market season.

new.title: Spend a day at the egapark
new.desc: Garden park on the Cyriaksberg, site of the 1961 international garden exhibition, with the Danakil desert and rainforest house opened for BUGA 2021.
new.tip: Admission is charged; open year-round, Mondays only in July and August.

new.title: Visit the Thüringer Zoopark Erfurt
new.desc: Zoo opened in 1959 with about 1,000 animals of 133 species and nearly 400,000 visitors in 2019.
new.tip: Bus line 30 or tram line 5 stops at the zoo.
new.q: Thüringer Zoopark Erfurt, Am Zoopark 1, Erfurt

new.title: Wander the Erfurt Christmas Market on Domplatz
new.desc: More than 200 wooden huts run from Domplatz via the Fischmarkt to the Anger, centred on a roughly 25 m tree in front of the cathedral. The 2026 market runs 24 November to 22 December.
new.tip: Go on a weekday evening to avoid the crush; try a Rostbratwurst from a stall.

new.title: Watch a show at the DomStufen-Festspiele
new.desc: Open-air musical theatre staged on the 70 sandstone steps in front of the cathedral and Severikirche, produced by Theater Erfurt since 1994. The 2026 production was Jesus Christ Superstar.
new.tip: Runs in August; book well ahead as seats sell out.

new.title: Join the Krämerbrückenfest
new.desc: Street festival around the Krämerbrücke held about the third weekend in June.
new.tip: Arrive on foot; the old town is crowded.

new.title: Tour Goethe's house on the Frauenplan
new.desc: The Goethe-Nationalmuseum and Goethe's residence opened as a museum on 8 August 1885 after the death of Goethe's last grandson. The complex was reorganised in 1999.
new.tip: Book timed tickets via the Klassik Stiftung.

new.title: Step into the Rococo Hall of Anna Amalia Library
new.desc: Founded in 1691, the library's oval three-storey Rococo hall survived a 2004 fire that destroyed about 50,000 volumes. It reopened in October 2007.
new.tip: Entry is by timed slots; book ahead.
new.q: Herzogin Anna Amalia Bibliothek, Platz der Demokratie 1, Weimar

new.title: See the world's oldest Bauhaus collection
new.desc: The Bauhaus-Museum opened in April 2019 and shows the oldest Bauhaus collection in the world.
new.tip: Pair it with Museum Neues Weimar nearby.

new.title: Visit Schiller's house on Schillerstraße
new.desc: Schiller moved into this 1777 house on 29 April 1802 and died there on 9 May 1805.
new.tip: Tickets via the Klassik Stiftung.

new.title: Pay respects in the Fürstengruft
new.desc: Goethe was buried here on 26 March 1832 beside Schiller at his own request. A 2008 gene test showed that the bones believed to be Schiller's were not his.
new.tip: Located in the Historischer Friedhof.

new.title: Visit Goethe's Gartenhaus in the Ilm park
new.desc: Goethe signed the purchase contract on 22 April 1776 and lived here before moving to Frauenplan in 1782. He kept visiting until February 1832.
new.tip: Best in spring when the garden blooms.
new.q: Goethes Gartenhaus, Park an der Ilm, Weimar

new.title: Discover Schloss Belvedere and its park
new.desc: Baroque palace built 1724 to 1748 for Duke Ernst August I, now a Rococo museum with orangery and grotto, part of the UNESCO ensemble Klassisches Weimar.
new.tip: About 4 km south of the centre; take the bus or cycle the Belvederer Allee.

new.title: See Haus Am Horn, the first Bauhaus building
new.desc: Built in about four months in 1923 as the Bauhaus model house, UNESCO World Heritage since 1996.
new.tip: Check opening days with the Bauhaus-Universität.
new.q: Haus Am Horn, Am Horn 61, Weimar

new.title: Visit the Buchenwald Memorial on the Ettersberg
new.desc: The memorial stands on the site of the Nazi concentration camp operated from July 1937, where around 56,000 of about 277,800 prisoners died.
new.tip: Allow half a day; bus line 6 runs from Weimar.

new.title: Order Thüringer Klöße at Scharfe Ecke
new.desc: Small Gasthaus known for dumplings made to order, which can take up to 20 minutes.
new.tip: Reserve; the room is small.

new.title: Eat Thüringer Klöße at Kartoffelhaus
new.desc: Potato-themed restaurant serving Thüringer Klöße in several versions, including with pork goulash and red cabbage.
new.tip: English-speaking staff.

new.title: Order Tafelspitz at Zum Weißen Schwan
new.desc: Gasthaus at Frauentorstraße 23 with over 450 years of history, known for Tafelspitz with horseradish.
new.tip: Close to the Goethe house.

new.title: Have coffee at the Residenz-Café
new.desc: Founded on 7 November 1839, said to be Weimar's oldest surviving coffee house; Goethe's first Weimar lodging was in the adjoining building.
new.tip: Sit by the window on Grüner Markt.

new.title: Eat in the town hall cellar at Erbenhof
new.desc: Cellar restaurant on Am Markt listed among Weimar's top restaurants by Fodor's.
new.tip: Try the Thuringian dishes.

new.title: Stroll the Park an der Ilm
new.desc: Landscape park begun in 1776 under Goethe's influence, with the Römisches Haus (1791 to 1798) and Goethe's Gartenhaus.
new.tip: Free and open year-round.

new.title: Join the Weimarer Zwiebelmarkt
new.desc: Folk festival on the second weekend of October, first mentioned in 1653, with about 600 stalls and Zwiebelkuchen with Federweißer.
new.tip: Arrive early; the old town is packed.

new.title: Ride up the JenTower for a city panorama
new.desc: Zeiss research tower built 1970 to 1972, now 159.6 m tall, with a restaurant and observation platform on floors 28 and 29.
new.tip: Check jentower.de for hours.

new.title: See the stars in the Zeiss-Planetarium
new.desc: Opened on 18 July 1926, the world's oldest large-dome projection planetarium still operating. It reopened on 15 July 2026 after a 7.5 million euro modernisation.
new.tip: Book a show in advance.

new.title: Climb to the Fuchsturm on the Hausberg
new.desc: Medieval tower on the 375 m Hausberg; burned in 1905 after lightning and its roof was removed in 1944.
new.tip: Combine with the Gaststätte beside it.

new.title: Wander the Botanischer Garten Jena
new.desc: Founded in 1586, the second-oldest botanical garden in Germany; Goethe sat on its supervising commission.
new.tip: Opposite the university library.

new.title: Visit the Phyletisches Museum
new.desc: Ernst Haeckel gave the building to the university on 30 July 1908; the first permanent exhibition opened in 1912.
new.tip: See the museum homepage for hours.
new.q: Phyletisches Museum, Vor dem Neutor 1, Jena

new.title: Visit Schillers Gartenhaus
new.desc: Schiller bought it in March 1797 for 1,050 Taler and had a small tower built there in 1798.
new.tip: Check hours before visiting.

new.title: Drink house-brewed beer at Braugasthof Papiermühle
new.desc: Brewpub in Jena-West with five beers brewed on site and Thuringian cooking.
new.tip: Open late; try the house beer with a Thuringian dish.

new.title: Eat regional food at Gasthaus zum Roten Hirsch
new.desc: Historic Gasthaus at Holzmarkt 10 with traditional Thuringian dishes and game.
new.tip: Mixed reviews; go for the regional classics.
new.q: Gasthaus zum Roten Hirsch, Holzmarkt 10, Jena

new.title: Eat Thuringian specialties at the Fuchsturm Gaststätte
new.desc: Hilltop Gaststätte with a beer garden by the tower.
new.tip: A reward after the climb.

new.title: Hang out at Café Wagner
new.desc: Cultural café and club on Wagnergasse with live music, films and board game nights.
new.tip: Check the programme.

new.title: See a gig at the Rosenkeller
new.desc: Student club in the cellars of Haus zur Rosen at Johannisstraße 13, opened on 3 May 1966.
new.tip: Check the programme.
